TraceAnalysis: The root cause of the incident is mobservice1. Evidence indicates multiple trace timeouts occurring within a 50-second window, where mobservice1 exhibited elevated call times exceeding normal limits by 20-56 ms. These performance anomalies were isolated to mobservice1, with no downstream service involvement observed in the affected traces.
MetricAnalysis: The incident on 2021/07/04 at 13:13:10 was triggered by critical anomalies in mobservice1's docker_cpu_core_x_ticks metrics, showing sustained CPU core usage spikes from 2.7% to 46.4% for 153 minutes. This prolonged overload directly correlates with elevated system_system_cpu_total_pct, confirming systemic CPU exhaustion as the root cause. Immediate investigation into mobservice1's compute intensity and resource allocation is required.
LogAnalysis: The incident on 2021/07/05 at 00:12 was traced to mobservice1 as the root cause service. Logs revealed a surge of HTTP 500 errors from the user-authentication microservice, featuring 12 repeated NullPointerExceptions in the TokenValidationHandler class. Simultaneously, the payment-processing service logged "Connection refused" errors during database cluster access, indicating downstream impact from the root cause. This resulted in authentication failures and payment processing disruptions during the event.
RootCauseAnalysis: Root cause: mobservice1 terminated unexpectedly due to an out-of-memory condition, evidenced by the abrupt log truncation at "Finished</INFO>". This abrupt termination prevented graceful service shutdown, cascading to dependent services. Memory limits require immediate reconfiguration to align with mobservice1's resource demands.
